headline: The control plane for your coding agents, however you run them.
description: An open-source control plane for coding agents. One checkout of rules, skills, roles and stances, projected into Claude Code and Codex with your own primitives, enforced with hooks, and measured with usage telemetry and cost controls. It layers under the rules libraries and orchestration you already use.
stances: Preferences you can switch: autonomy, delegation, cost, testing, voice, commits, planning, licensing and build versus buy. Three of those bind to enforcement today: autonomy sets which shell-command grade stops and asks, delegation changes spawn routing, and cost resolves a model and budget table per role. The rest are prose that swaps cleanly. The usage report groups rule hits by the variant that was selected, so a switch can be checked rather than assumed.
github_description: The control plane for your coding agents, however you run them. One checkout of rules, skills, subagents, hooks and stances, projected into Claude Code and Codex with your own primitives: hook-enforced guardrails, usage telemetry, cost postures and model tiering, under any rules library or orchestration layer.

hero.title: The control plane for your coding agents, however you run them.
hero.subtitle: Model Citizen sits under the Claude Code and Codex you already run, and under whatever rules library you like. It keeps your rules, skills, roles and stances in one checkout, projects them into each agent with your own primitives, enforces them with hooks, and shows you what every session did and what it cost.
hero.proof: MIT licensed. One checkout, nothing hosted, and citizen uninstall puts everything back. Every release names the clients it qualified and what it could not prove.

capabilities.title: Guardrails that leave room for judgment
capabilities.pitch: Hooks handle the few things that should be deterministic, and each has an id you can switch off; the four that enforce need your acknowledgement first. Everything else stays the agent's call.

features.name: Graded shell commands
features.line: Every command is graded from read-only to irreversible, and your autonomy stance, plus any per-repository levels in a local policy, decides which grades stop and ask.

features.name: Stop gate
features.line: The turn doesn't end while your repo's own gate is red.

features.name: Fresh-context review
features.line: Scope is checked against the ask, then quality, by agents that never saw the code, and a framework's own review spawns are held to that whatever they call themselves.

features.name: Secrets and personal data
features.line: Lint catches tokens, keys and personal strings before they're committed.

features.name: Untrusted tool output
features.line: Text that comes back from a tool is data, never instructions.

features.name: Sandboxing
features.line: Fence the filesystem and network before you leave a loop unattended.

capabilities.title: Settings you own, on every runtime you run
capabilities.pitch: Sync keeps a journal of what it changed and refuses to overwrite what it does not own. Uninstall puts it back. The same rules then go to both runtimes.

features.name: Reversible
features.line: Sync has a dry run, diff shows drift, an ownership journal records prior and applied values, and uninstall restores what it adopted.

features.name: Shared primitives
features.line: Rules, skills, roles and workflows live in one place and sync into each runtime's native settings. Switch one off and sync leaves it out of both.

features.name: Same policy on both
features.line: A Claude Code spawn and a Codex spawn resolve to the same delegation policy.

features.name: Declared integrations
features.line: A planning framework declares itself in one descriptor. citizen integration check|apply installs its overrides, and the spawn hook confines its review layers.

features.name: Honest compatibility
features.line: The catalog says which clients are qualified and where the gaps are: two runtimes today, and the headline does not claim more.

features.name: Worktrees and workspaces
features.line: Each agent works in its own worktree and claims the paths it writes. Your .code-workspace files decide which repositories a session sees, instructions included.

capabilities.title: See and steer what your agents spend
capabilities.pitch: A hard cap cuts an agent off after it has already spent the tokens. I'd rather tell it what things cost and let it pace itself.

features.name: Cost postures
features.line: Pick frugal, balanced or max, or write your own. One table sets model, effort and a soft budget per role.

features.name: Model tiering
features.line: Roles ask for a capability class, one of frontier, strong, standard and light, not a model name. Gathering files doesn't run on the model that reviews your code.

features.name: Band workers
features.line: A spawn that names no role gets a right-sized worker instead of your most expensive model.

features.name: A budget in every brief
features.line: Each subagent is told its expected tokens and tool calls. Finish if you're close, otherwise return what you have.

features.name: Live usage feed
features.line: The orchestrator sees what each turn and each subagent cost, and hears once when its context passes the size your stance sets. A decision log records what a hook decided.

features.name: Lean context
features.line: Always-loaded instructions are capped at 225 lines, and lint fails the commit past that. Noisy tool output is filtered before it lands in the transcript.

capabilities.title: Answers and plans you can actually read
capabilities.pitch: Most agent output is a wall of text. This puts the verdict first and the ask where you can find it.

features.name: Voice stances
features.line: Choose concise, answer-card or scannable. Same content, shaped for how you read.

features.name: Scannable output style
features.line: Verdict first, action items in one place, and status in plain words: Fixed, Partially fixed, Not fixed, Unverified.

features.name: Review Card plans
features.line: Every plan opens with a one-screen card, rendered in the native plan pane and approved there rather than by a typed reply.

features.name: Bounded subagent returns
features.line: Subagents come back with findings and a word cap, not their whole transcript.

features.name: Conciseness rules
features.line: Explain a decision once. Comments say why, not what.

capabilities.title: Rules you can measure, and prune
capabilities.pitch: Every project in this field writes instructions and hopes. Here a rule nobody can observe is a rule nobody can prune, and lint says so before the commit lands.

features.name: Detector or reason
features.line: Every rule names a deterministic detector over the transcript, or says in one line why nothing in a transcript can decide it. Lint fails the commit otherwise.

features.name: Hit rate per rule
features.line: citizen usage --rules reports how often each rule fired, by repository and by the variant you had selected; --by profile splits spend by the profile behind each row.

features.name: Cache prefix held
features.line: citizen usage --by prefix reports each session's cache-miss ratio and names the turn where it jumped. It measures the prefix; nothing denies a change.

features.name: What is detected
features.line: Nineteen deterministic detectors read the transcript: whole-file reads, unverified pushes, secrets in a write, banned openers, non-conventional commits.

features.name: Caught in the act
features.line: The instrument has already caught two of this repository's own shipped features doing nothing. Both are filed as issues, not hidden.

features.name: Exports where you already look
features.line: The same ledger exports over OTLP, off by default, to Langfuse, Phoenix or Opik, adding the one thing they cannot see: which rule fired.

capabilities.title: Your preferences, as switches
capabilities.pitch: Reasonable developers disagree about testing, autonomy and how much to delegate. Nine axes, each a named choice: three bind to enforcement today, the rest are prose that swaps cleanly.

features.name: Stance dimensions and variants
features.line: Autonomy, delegation, testing, cost, voice, commits, planning, licensing and build versus buy.

features.name: User, project, session
features.line: Set a default or pick a mode, override it for one repo or session, and the agent follows the override from its next session. citizen selection shows what set each unit.

features.name: Write your own
features.line: A new stance dimension is a folder of Markdown files. No fork needed.

features.name: See one switch end to end
features.line: The demo flips delegation and shows what changes in both runtimes.

features.name: Autonomy stances
features.line: Execute, confirm-writes or ask. The choice sets which shell-command grade stops and asks; it is enforced, not advised.

features.name: Judgment stays local by default
features.line: An external judgment provider is off at every decision point until you turn it on, sends only the fields you list, and one file switches every call off.

on_the_way.title: Measured against bare
on_the_way.line: Proof set 1 runs the harness against bare Claude Code, and harness evidence verify re-derives every published figure from its rows, whatever they show.

on_the_way.title: The superpowers mode
on_the_way.line: One switch hands planning and testing to Superpowers while every hook stays on, and doctor names the mode when it finds the plugin.
